strengths: The paper presents a novel and well-motivated solution by introducing attention-driven dynamic masking. Unlike previous works using fixed or random masking, PointACL adaptively masks high-attention regions to force learning from under-attended areas.
The paper provides extensive experimental evidence to support its claims, including thorough robustness analysis under various perturbations (Gaussian noise, rotation, scaling, point dropout).
This paper is well-written and easy to read.
The motivation that employing an attention-driven dynamic masking strategy to enhance the understanding of global structures within the point cloud is reasonable.

In my opinion, the paper is well written and clear. The problem statement and the proposed solutions are well explained and presented. I particularly appreciated the plot showing the attended regions, showing that the proposed framework indeed learns a more global understanding of the input point cloud.
Results are good, and I think the main takeaway from this paper is that giving more importance to less prominent patches yields very robust results to perturbations.
The paper is easy to follow.
The motivation is interesting and the visualization is helpful.
weaknesses: The paper lacks theoretical analysis or justification for why the attention-driven dynamic masking strategy works. There's no mathematical foundation explaining: Why masking high-attention regions leads to better global understanding? How the dynamic probability distribution affects learning? What properties of the contrastive loss ensure better feature discrimination. This theoretical gap makes it difficult to understand the method's fundamental principles and potentially limits its generalizability.
The paper primarily compares with Point-MAE and PointGPT-S as backbones, but misses comparisons with other masking strategies from recent works.
The performance improvement of this paper on few shot learning and part segmentation tasks is not significant.

Innovations are limited. The method simply generates an attention-guided masked point cloud, and adds the comparative loss of the original point patches and masked point patches on original loss function.

Improvements over baseline methods are quite marginal and perhaps not statistically significant. While this method can be seamlessly integrated into mainstream transformer architectures, it remains unclear whether the performance gains are due to additional 300 epoch pre-training, an increase in parameters, or the dynamic masking strategy itself.
It has not achieved SOTA performance and is not compared with the latest methods，such as PointMamba [1], Point-FEMAE[2],  Point-GPT-L.

The author did not demonstrate the generality of the proposed method. Assuming that this dynamic masking strategy is effective, it should be applicable to all transformer-based point cloud models, such as Point BERT, Point-FEMAE, Point-GPT-L etc. The author lacks further analysis of the generality of the proposed ideas.
Is there any comparison of computational efficiency and cost with baseline?
The improvement is slight, especially for part segmentation (only 0.1 for Ins. mIoU)
